study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Wolfers et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2021
study_identification_part.si4_title: Replicating extensive brain structural heterogeneity in individuals with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Replicate prior findings that group-level differences mask substantial individual-level heterogeneity by applying normative modeling to VBM gray matter maps in independent TOP samples of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.

rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: All participants were recruited as part of the Thematically Organized Psychosis (TOP) study, approved by the Regional Committee for Medical Research Ethics and the Norwegian Data Inspectorate (Doan et al., 2017). The two replication samples were selected from the TOP-database on the 25th of September 2019.

rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: Structural scans were obtained on 1.5 Tesla Siemens MAGNETOM Sonata scanner...; Structural scans were obtained on 3 Tesla GE 750 Discovery scanner...; Structural scans were obtained on 3 Tesla GE Signa HDxT...; As in our previous article, we estimated the normative model using Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to predict VBM based regional gray matter volumes across the brain from age and sex.; Note here, that if you replicate these findings in a sample on multiple scanners using different scanning sequences your interpretation might be misguided due to scanning confounds. clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Robust group-level differences coexist with marked individual-level heterogeneity; only a small proportion of patients show extreme deviations in the same regions, replicating prior findings across two independent samples.
